name: Discman
blurb: Sony's portable CD player from 1984, and the anti-skip players that followed
title: Sony Discman: When It Came Out, Anti-Skip and What Happened
description: The Discman was Sony's portable CD player, launched in Japan in November 1984 as the D-50. Renamed CD Walkman by 2000, it faded with MP3 players and the iPod.
answer: The Discman was Sony's line of portable CD players, starting with the D-50, launched in Japan in November 1984 for 49,800 yen, about $350 at the time. With headphones and batteries, it let you carry CDs the way the Walkman had carried cassettes, though early models skipped whenever they were jolted. Sony renamed the line CD Walkman by 2000 and phased it out around the early 2010s; other companies still make portable CD players.

body: A Discman was a flat round box a little larger than a CD itself, with a lid that flipped up so you could drop the disc onto a spindle. The D-50 was designed to be about the size of four CD cases stacked together, which was tiny for a CD player in 1984. It had no batteries inside: it ran from a mains adapter or a battery pack clipped to it, while later models took ordinary AA cells.

The big problem was skipping. A CD player reads the disc with a laser as it spins, so walking, running or a bus going over a bump could knock the laser off track and the music would stutter. Many people carried a Discman flat in both hands, or kept it still on a desk.

The fix was buffer memory, sold under names such as ESP (Electronic Shock Protection), Anti-Shock and later Sony's G-Protection. The player read the disc ahead of time and stored the audio in memory, so if a jolt interrupted reading, it kept playing from memory while the laser found its place again. When the feature first appeared in the early 1990s, about 3 seconds of buffer was the maximum; later players held 10 seconds or more. Early anti-skip could cut battery life by up to half.

body: Sony no longer makes portable CD players; its current Walkman products are digital music players. Old Discmans and CD Walkmans circulate second-hand. With CD sales growing again in the mid-2020s, other brands have released new portable CD players, some with Bluetooth, so the format itself is still available.

faq.q: When did the Discman come out?
faq.a: The first model, the Sony D-50, launched in Japan in November 1984.

faq.q: Why did portable CD players skip?
faq.a: A laser reads the spinning disc, and a bump could knock it off track. Anti-skip memory solved this by storing a few seconds of music ahead.

faq.q: Is a Discman the same as a CD Walkman?
faq.a: Yes. Both are Sony portable CD players; Sony switched from the Discman name to CD Walkman between 1997 and 2000.
